title: Why Did T. Rex Have Such Tiny Arms?
sources: Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History: T. rex

beats.say: T. rex was a giant dinosaur. But its arms were super tiny! Why?
Hi! I'm Milo. Let's fly way back in time to the dinosaurs!
T. rex's arms were so short, they couldn't even reach its mouth!
Scientists are still finding out what those little arms were for. It's a dino mystery!
But T. rex had a super nose. Scientists think it could smell things far, far away.
Can you wiggle tiny T. rex arms? Be kind to every animal. See you at the zoo!

title: T. Rex Never Met Stegosaurus! Here's Why
sources: Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History: Stegosaurus

beats.say: T. rex and Stegosaurus never met. Not even once! How come?
Hi! I'm Milo. Let's fly way back in time to the dinosaurs!
Stegosaurus lived about 150 million years ago. T. rex came much, much later.
So T. rex actually lived closer in time to us than to Stegosaurus! Wow!
Stegosaurus had big plates on its back, and a spiky tail called a thagomizer!
Can you say thagomizer? Be kind to every animal. See you at the zoo!

title: Brachiosaurus Was Taller Than a House!

beats.say: Can you reach the top of a tree? Brachiosaurus could! How?
Hi! I'm Milo. Let's fly way back in time to the dinosaurs!
Brachiosaurus had a super long neck, and it was taller than a house!
Its front legs were longer than its back legs, like a giraffe.
It stretched up high to munch leaves at the very top of the trees.
Can you stretch up tall like Brachiosaurus? Be kind to every animal. See you at the zoo!

title: Pteranodon Was NOT a Dinosaur!
sources: Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History: Pterosaurs

beats.say: It flew with giant wings in dinosaur times. But it was not a dinosaur! What was it?
Hi! I'm Milo. Let's fly way back in time to the dinosaurs!
This is Pteranodon. It was a flying reptile called a pterosaur.
Its wings were wider than a car! It soared high over the sea.
Its name means toothless wing, because it had no teeth at all!
Can you flap your arms like giant wings? Be kind to every animal. See you at the zoo!
You taste with your tongue. A butterfly tastes with its feet! Really?
Hi! I'm Milo. Let's fly to the garden for a bug hunt!
Yes! Butterflies have tiny tasters on their feet.
When a butterfly lands on a leaf, its feet tell it if the leaf is good.
And every butterfly starts out as a little caterpillar!
Can you flutter like a butterfly? Be kind to every animal. See you at the zoo!

title: Honeybees DANCE to Talk to Friends!
sources: USDA Agricultural Research Service: Honey bees

beats.say: How do bees tell their friends where the best flowers are? They dance!
Hi! I'm Milo. Let's fly to the garden for a bug hunt!
A honeybee does a wiggly dance called the waggle dance.
The dance shows the other bees which way to fly to find the flowers.
And bees have five eyes! Two big ones, and three tiny ones on top.
Can you do a waggle dance? Be kind to every animal. See you at the zoo!

title: Where Are a Snail's Eyes? Look Up!

beats.say: Your eyes are on your face. Where are a snail's eyes? Look up!
Hi! I'm Milo. Let's fly to the garden for a bug hunt!
A garden snail's eyes sit at the tips of its long tentacles!
It can pull them in and pop them back out. Peekaboo!
A snail slides on a slippery trail of slime. Slow and steady!
Can you slide slowly like a snail? Be kind to every animal. See you at the zoo!

title: Ants Can Carry Things Heavier Than Themselves!

beats.say: Could you carry a car? An ant can carry things much heavier than its own body!
Hi! I'm Milo. Let's fly to the garden for a bug hunt!
Ants are tiny, but they are super strong!
An ant can lift a leaf or a crumb that is heavier than itself.
And ants talk to each other with smells, and by touching their antennae.
Can you show me your strong muscles? Be kind to every animal. See you at the zoo!
